ideas.name: long_horn_tip_linkage
ideas.description: The tip_tongue with its two-servo tip linkage rebuilt: 1.5x longer printed servo horns and a moved ball-link pivot. The same MG90S servos then move the tip blade about 1.5x farther per degree. Torque at the blade drops to about 2/3, which is still enough to press the silicone blade shut against the 1.2 cm bore. Servo noise at the blade grows by the same 1.5x, so the s channel (0.05-0.15 cm2) gets touchier.
ideas.test: Add a tip-linkage gain parameter (degrees per cm of tip travel) to tip_tongue, ranging over about 0.65-1.0x the current value, and re-run ta, t, s and sh.

ideas.name: high_speed_tip_servo
ideas.description: Replace tip servo 1 of the tip_tongue linkage with a high-speed metal-gear micro servo (e.g. a helicopter tail-rotor class part, about 0.05 s/60° at 5 V, 9 g, MG90S footprint and spline). It mounts on the same horn and pushrod and uses the same controller channel, so the servo count stays at 6 of 6. The linkage geometry and the tip's 0.3-5 cm place range and 0-1.3 height range are unchanged, so every held posture is reproduced exactly. Only the transition time falls by half. The 32° tip release then takes about 27 ms. If the drawstring is also swapped (a second unit, budget permitting later), the 53° clean pair takes about 44 ms. Both fit the 50 ms window, so the release is heard as a stop, not a glide.
ideas.test: The simulator needs a servo speed attribute for each channel, so the syllable check can be judged on transition time (50 ms) instead of a fixed 30° per MG90S. The tip servo 1 channel would be set to 0.05 s/60°.

ideas.name: differential_tip_linkage
ideas.description: This replaces tip_tongue's two-servo tip linkage with a printed differential bellcrank. Both MG90S servos drive a common rocker through ball-link pushrods. Turning the servos together raises or lowers the blade, and turning them in opposition slides it along the palate between 0.3 and 5 cm. The blade, the body pad, the rail and the cam are reused unchanged. A height change at fixed place is shared equally between the two servos, so the /t/ release (Δheight of about 0.65) costs each servo about half of today's 32°. The workspace becomes a diamond: full height is available across about 0.3-3.5 cm of place, which covers t, s and sh.
ideas.test: A tip_tongue variant whose tip controls (tip_height, tip_place) map to servo angles through θ1 = a·h + b·p and θ2 = a·h − b·p. Choose a so the full 1.3 height spans about 153° of θ1+θ2 combined (about 76° per servo), and choose b so the 4.7 cm of place spans the remaining throw. Then rerun ta, t, s and sh, and check the largest per-servo turn on the ta closure-to-vowel pair.

ideas.name: glottal_offset_pad_carriage
ideas.description: A printed offset arm on the tip_tongue body carriage. It carries the cam follower and silicone pad 1.0 cm toward the glottis from the rail carriage, instead of having the carriage trail 2.5 cm behind the pad. The cam stays on the carriage and lifts the pad through a short printed rocker on the arm, so the stroke (1.3 cm) and the cam servo's turn are unchanged. The carriage's clearance to the reed housing is the same as today, but the pad itself can descend to about 1.5 cm above the glottis. That opens a low-pharynx constriction, which raises F1 and lowers F2 for /ɑ/ on a shortened 13.0 cm cast. The tip blade linkage is untouched, so t, s and sh keep their mechanics.
ideas.test: In the simulator, cut the tip_tongue sled clearance from 2.5 cm behind the pad to 1.5 cm, so the pad may reach 1.5 cm above the glottis. Then run tract length 13.0 with rail_start 4.0 and stroke 1.3: the pad reaches 11.0 cm behind the teeth, 2.0 cm above the glottis. Re-fit ta and check ka, iy, uw, er and aa.

proposals.principle: A stop needs an articulator that seals the bore at its place, and a fricative needs a channel narrower than a vowel's but wider than a seal. The cam lift sets how far the pad presses into the 1.2 cm bore radius. Above 1.2 cm the pad squeezes the tube shut, so a 1.3 cm lift spans both the 0.05-0.15 cm2 channel range and a full seal.
proposals.hypothesis: The stroke is 0.95 cm, and 0.95 is short of the 1.2 cm radius. That is the only reason the smallest area is 0.20 cm2. Raising it to 1.3 cm (the top of the range) lets System 1 seal at the velar place for /k/. It also lets it hold a 0.05-0.15 cm2 channel near 3.1-3.5 cm, where System 1's best /ʃ/ posture already sits and its hiss already peaks at 3211 Hz, inside 2000-4000 Hz. I keep rail_start at 3.25 so the pad still reaches 10.25 cm, which /ɑ/ and the other back vowels use. This costs nothing to buy and is the cheapest move that fixes the cause rather than the symptom.
risks: iy, ih: with a larger lift, a high-front posture can tighten past the 0.15 cm2 vowel floor, which makes F1 sensitive to noise. The control range just extends to 1.3, so the old 0-0.95 postures are still available and System 1 can stay at them.
aa, ah, ae: the back-constriction postures they use are unchanged and still in range.

iterations.notes:
I'm sending three proposals. In order of cost:

1. **Params: stroke 1.3 (free).** The tongue can't seal or form a fricative channel because its 0.95 cm lift is less than the 1.2 cm bore radius. Raising the lift to 1.3 cm should gain /k/ and /ʃ/.
2. **Swap the tongue for tip_tongue, with stroke 1.3 ($12, 3 days, 76 machine min).** Nothing reaches 0-1.5 cm behind the teeth, so the tongue needs a tip blade. This should gain /t/ and /s/, and also /tɑ/, because the body pad can hold the /ɑ/ shape through the /t/ closure.
3. **Swap the lips for round_lips, protrusion 1.6 ($4, 2 days, 57 machine min).** The lips never close below 3.00 cm2 and can't push forward. Closing and protruding them should gain /p/ and pull F2 down for /u/, /ʊ/ and /ɔ/.

Proposals 1 and 2 change the same slot, so whichever does better is the one that can be combined with 3. The tip_tongue and round_lips swaps together cost $16, need 3 days of lead time (bought in parallel) and 133 machine minutes, all within budget, and use exactly 6 of the 6 controller channels.

I'm keeping the tract as it is this round. Lengthening it (long_cast, 203 machine min) moves every formant at once, which risks the six held vowels. I'd rather first see how much rounding fixes the low F2.

/ɝ/ (low F3) probably needs constrictions at the tip, the body and the lips together, and only becomes possible if both swaps are kept. I'm not predicting it this round.

I'm proposing one change this round. It's an idea, so it gets recorded and costed but not tried in the simulator.

**Why not a parameter move:** the record has already covered this. Tract length 13.0, 12.75 and 13.25 all raise F1 and F2 together. Rail_start 3.7 and 4.0 move the pad deeper, and the deepest legal pairing (13.0 cast with rail_start 4.0) was refused because the sled would hit the glottis hardware. Nothing else in the current parts' ranges addresses the coupling: stroke must stay above 1.2 to seal /k/, and max_protrusion is already at its 1.6 maximum.

- jaw_lips and spread_lips have a 2.5-3.5 cm2 rest gap, so they can't seal and would lose /p/.
- long_rail_tongue has no tip, so it would lose t, s and sh.
- long_cast drops the F1 ceiling to about 656 Hz, so it would lose aa.

A deeper pad together with the 13.0 cast should let /ɑ/ hold its F1 with the tip near its seal, so the release needs less tip servo turn.

**Cost:** $0, 0 days and about 15 machine minutes (10 g PLA and 2 g silicone), all from the manifest. It leaves the $16 budget untouched.

iterations.notes:
The only failing group is ta. Its mechanism is transition_too_slow: tip servo 1 turns 32°, and the limit is 30°.

The cause is a tight formant window. /ɑ/ needs F1 at 657 Hz or more, but at the tip height the release allows it only reaches 647. F2 is 1148 against a 1199 ceiling, and the brief's lowest F2 when F1 is 650-900 Hz is 1118.

The record brackets the tract length:
- 13.5 cm fails because F1 is too low.
- 13.0 cm fails because F2 sits at its ceiling.
- 12.75 cm also loses iy.
- Moving the pad deeper hits the sled rule, or loses ka on servo noise (rail_start 3.7 and 3.75).

So I am proposing untried lengths inside that bracket (13.1, 13.2, and 13.25 with rail_start 3.5).

No catalogue swap can do this without breaking a held group:
- jaw_lips and spread_lips have a 2.5 cm2 rest gap, so they cannot seal the lips and p is lost.
- The cam and long-rail tongues have no tip, so t, s and sh are lost.
- long_cast lowers F1.
- larynx_tube costs $23, over the $16 left.
- pneumatic_tongue needs a valve manifold that cannot be bought.

If none of these is kept, the real fix is one of the linkage ideas already recorded, costing $0 and about 26 machine minutes. long_horn_tip_linkage or differential_tip_linkage would cut tip servo 1's degrees per cm of tip travel, and that addresses the 32° directly.

- A tract recast takes about 165 machine minutes.
- A tongue recast takes about 76.
- Any one proposal fits in the 468 minutes left.
